# Standard-library vulnerabilities the Nix channel is known to carry, and
# which are accepted rather than fixed.
#
# Why they exist: the flake builds with whatever Go nixpkgs ships, while the
# four GoReleaser channels build with the newest patch (#70). nixpkgs lands a
# Go patch release the same day upstream tags it, but the bump rides the
# staging -> staging-next -> master train, which historically takes 13 to 23
# days to reach nixos-unstable. So this channel trails the archives on
# standard-library patches, permanently and by roughly a fortnight. See #69.
#
# Why they are accepted rather than fixed: every entry below is denial of
# service or self-XSS, none yields code execution, and none can produce a
# fail-open update. Pinning a newer Go by hand would be obsolete within the
# fortnight and would then silently hold the channel *behind* nixpkgs.
#
# How to change this file: entries come out when a scan stops finding them.
# Nothing goes in without the reachability judgement that the ones below got.
#
# last confirmed: 2026-08-19

# Reached through http.Client redirect handling, so it needs a registry you
# already trust to answer with a malicious Location header. Burns CPU.
GO-2026-6218

# Rendered data reaches html/template from the state DB, originating in
# Compose files and registry responses. Every route is behind `guard`, the
# bind defaults to 127.0.0.1:7476, and the UI is read-only -- so the worst
# case is XSS in the operator's own browser.
GO-2026-6091

# Needs Ripen to be a TLS *server*. It never is: the Web UI serves plain HTTP
# by design and all TLS is client-side. No primitive.
GO-2026-6090

# Needs unencrypted HTTP/2. The Web UI enables no such thing and already sets
# ReadHeaderTimeout. No primitive.
GO-2026-6089

# encoding/xml is not imported anywhere in the tree. Unreachable.
GO-2026-6088

# The sharpest of the eight: crypto/x509 parses the peer's DER before the pin
# and CA checks in internal/portainer, so a hostile chain crashes the process.
# The peer is the Portainer host the operator configured.
GO-2026-5972

# Affected symbol is net.LookupCNAME, which Ripen never calls, and it does no
# DNS parsing of its own.
GO-2026-5942

# The hostname checks it would bypass all fail closed against a Punycode
# label, and every hostname is operator-supplied policy. No bypass primitive.
GO-2026-5026
